title: Theta Lift of a K Type Datum
body_html:
Theta Lift of a K Type Datum

A \(K\)-type datum \(\Sigma'\) is a theta lift of a supercuspidal datum \(\Sigma\) for the dual pair \((U(V),U(V'))\) when:

  • \(\Sigma\) is decomposed into blocks as a \(K\)-type datum.
  • Each positive-depth block of \(\Sigma'\) is obtained from the corresponding block of \(\Sigma\) by the single positive-depth lift \(\#^+\).
  • The zero-depth block of \(\Sigma'\) is a finite-field theta lift of the zero-depth block of \(\Sigma\), without requiring supercuspidality.
  • The target datum is the direct sum of all target blocks.

This definition is used in the proof of the main theorem because intermediate oscillator-model \(K\)-types need not all be supercuspidal, even when the final first-occurrence representation is.
